description:
FILED s543k (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22), found by member 6's probe f10 (#5370: the block spellings that must stay blocks).  PRE-EXISTING: base 4a0fd0ec the same; `${"1"}` (a STRING) is right.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl):
    "abc" =~ /(b)/; no strict "refs"; my $one = 1;
    print ${ +1 }, "|", ${"1"}, "|", ${ $one }, "\n";
        perl  b|b|b        PCL  1|b|1

WHAT IT IS: the scalar cast of a non-reference NUMBER returns the number itself instead of stringifying it and reading the variable of that name (perl: rv2sv of a non-ref is a symbolic reference by its STRING value).  Suspect: p-cast-$ / %p-symref-box's dispatch has a number arm that answers the value.  Rule 12 read of that dispatch owed.
=== DONE (s543m, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) -- the RAW-number half; the boxed half is #551 ===
THE RULE-12 READ of p-cast-$'s dispatch: a number falls to `(t inner)` and is answered as itself BY DESIGN (#505 / #551, measured s446j, ruled s335 "no new box slot"): a BOX holding a number is byte for byte a referent box handed out of a container (`${ $h{k} }` with `$h{k} = \42` must read 42), so a boxed number cannot be called symbolic.  A RAW number is a different case: a hard reference never reaches p-cast-$ unboxed (probed: `\42` through a hash, an array, a sub return, a foreach alias, @_, map, eval -- all arrive boxed), so a raw number is perl's rv2sv of a non-reference.
THE FIX: p-cast-$ reads a raw number as the symbolic name of its STRING (strict refs' fatal through the string arm), and (setf p-cast-$) writes through it (`${ +1 } = 5` now dies "Modification of a read-only value" -- it died "Cannot dereference non-reference" before; the place is right either way).  Reached: `${ +1 }` `${ 1.5 }` `${ +0 }` `${ 3 - 2 }` `${ $n + 1 }` `${ num() }`, and `${ $one }` / `$$one` when `$one` is a RAW-SLOT lexical (VarAnnotator's verdict: the common `my $one = 1`).  NOT reached: `${ $one }` when `$one` is boxed (a reference taken, `\$one`) -- #551; a design that would reach it is a compile-time "the operand is a my-declared, non-alias scalar" fact (a foreach alias, `$_`, an @_ element can each be a referent box), not taken.
PROBES: scratch/s543m/p5/m5.pl 8 lines: base 2, tree 8; p5/m5b.pl 4 lines: base 2, tree 3 (the boxed `${ $one }`).  `@{ $two }` / `%{ $n }` / `&{ $n }` were right on the base.  s543k's `${1}` (#5370) unchanged.
GUARD: Pl/t/symref-package-01.t row 20 (FAILS on the base).  Commit 5d646c3f (WIP 5).
